text: The Documents letters of the policy pack are taken from the legacy authority table under matrix version PM-2026.12: DOCUMENTS C for RW-RESTRUCT, RW-CASEOWN and SY-CASEWF, DOCUMENTS R for RW-TEAMMGR, and no DOCUMENTS row for RW-PHONECOL.
why: The TSD P4 RBAC matrix carries no Documents column, so the letters have to be fixed as a default before the build or the story cannot be estimated; the legacy story is the story master for its own authority table.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-026 sections 10 and 16; FSD P4 v3 A2.4; TSD P4 v3 T3.2 LOV-CAPABILITY and T6.1
applied_in: Section 3 Preconditions; section 7 AC1 and AC2; section 8 BR1 and BR2; section 10 Authority; section 12.8 Contract fakes
confirm: Security administrator and the business lead at the PM-2026.12 policy pack review
impact: A different letter set changes policy pack rows and two test cases only; no code change, because the letters are data.

text: POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise takes the actor reference (a user reference or a service identity), the roles the session resolved, the capability area, the right, the case and treatment reference, the template code list, the request key and the field IDs the screen will render, and answers the decision, the roles that carry the letter, the scope that was applied, the matrix version, the masking version, the masked marker per field ID and the messageId on a refusal.
why: Architecture v5 names the authorise operation and the TSD appendix does not, so the request and the answer have to be fixed as a default before the build; leaving them empty would stop the story.
read: Arch v5 slide 14 and slide 41; TSD P4 v3 T-A.1, T-A.2 API-P4-012 and T6.2; FSD P4 v3 A2.4 and A2.7; Legacy RWB-E2-026 sections 3, 4 and 12
applied_in: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 2 to 6 and 9 to 11; section 7 AC1 to AC9; section 12.1 and 12.8 Contract; section 13 Build steps 1 to 3
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-access tech lead when RWB-P4-E1037-CON and RWB-P5-E2026-CON are published
impact: A different shape changes the controller, the contract fakes and every caller client; the decision codes, the entry and the messages stay as specified.

text: The role row of the service identity SY-CASEWF is of role_class NON_HUMAN_ACTOR with DOCUMENTS C and default_scope ALL, and it passes exactly the same letter, scope and masking checks as a person, with no bypass path.
why: NFR-051 makes a service identity subject to the same checks and the legacy story needs the identity to generate, but no source binds a Documents letter, a class or a scope to SY-CASEWF, so a default is required.

confirm: Security administrator and the solution architect at the policy pack review
impact: If the pack gives the identity a narrower scope, only the policy row and AC4 change, because the check is the same code for every role class.

why: The sources fix that the field is masked and logged as masked but give no version label, no rows and no format for a national ID number, so a default is needed to answer and to record.

why: FSD P4 A2.7 fixes an entry per access event and legacy RWB-E2-026 BR8 generates a set whole or not at all, but no source says whether the entry belongs to the request or to each document, and the idempotency key of the legacy endpoint is per request.
